question.text:
How do plants excrete gaseous waste?
(A) Through root hairs
(B) Through stomata and lenticels
(C) Through xylem
(D) Through fruits

Waste products like latex and gums are stored in
(A) Old xylem
(B) Old phloem
(C) New xylem
(D) New phloem

What is the function of the glomerulus of the nephron?
(A) Filtration of blood.
(B) Re-absorption of ions from blood.
(C) Re-absorption of hormones from blood.
(D) Re-absorption of water from blood.

In plants, excess water is removed by:
(A) Transpiration
(B) Photosynthesis
(C) Diffusion
(D) Active transport

What is the primary function of an artificial kidney?
(A) To store excess blood
(B) To remove nitrogenous waste from the blood
(C) To produce urine artificially
(D) To increase blood pressure

Urine is finally excreted out of the body through the:
(A) Ureter
(B) Urethra
(C) Bladder
(D) Nephron

The function of Bowman's capsule is to:
(A) Store urine
(B) Reabsorb water
(C) Collect filtrate from blood
(D) Excrete nitrogenous waste

What is the role of the dialysing fluid in hemodialysis?
(A) It helps in blood clotting
(B) It prevents infections in the kidney
(C) It removes waste by diffusion
(D) It increases urine production

In unicellular organisms, excretion occurs by:
(A) Active transport
(B) Osmosis
(C) Diffusion
(D) Transpiration
